Robitussin helps to loosen congestion in your chest, making it easier to cough out. It can be used to relieve symptoms when you have a cold or allergies.

Robitussin DM contains two active ingredients, dextromethorphan and guaifenesin. Dextromethorphan relieves coughing by decreasing activity in your brain that gives you the urge to cough. Guaifenesin helps to loosen up mucus in your throat and lungs causing chest congestion.

As soon as dextromethorphan enters the blood stream, it starts to work with your body. This usually happens around 15 minutes of ingestion. The peak efficiency of the medicine occurs at 2 hours.

## Key takeaways

[Mucinex DM](https://www.goodrx.com/mucinex-dm/what-is)(guaifenesin / dextromethorphan) and [Delsym](https://www.goodrx.com/dextromethorphan/what-is) (dextromethorphan) are both over-the-counter medications used to relieve coughs caused by minor throat or lung irritation, such as the common cold. They both contain dextromethorphan, which is an antitussive or cough suppressant. However, Mucinex DM also includes guaifenesin, an expectorant that helps loosen mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough out. Mucinex DM is available in various forms, including tablets, oral liquids, and dissolvable granules, while Delsym is available as an extended-release syrup and immediate-release caplets. Mucinex DM is typically taken every 4 to 12 hours depending on the formulation, whereas Delsym is taken every 6 to 12 hours. Both medications can cause drowsiness, but Mucinex DM may also cause dizziness and stomach upset. You should avoid taking either medication with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) due to the risk of serotonin syndrome. Additionally, Mucinex DM should not be taken with other products containing dextromethorphan to prevent overdose.

### Mucinex DM

### Summary for Mucinex DM

Over-the-counter

Mucinex DM (guaifenesin / dextromethorphan) is an over-the-counter medication that's used to relieve [cough](https://www.goodrx.com/conditions/cough) and loosen mucus. It has two active ingredients: **guaifenesin** (an expectorant that clears chest congestion) and **dextromethorphan** (a cough suppressant that relieves cough). The medication is available as tablets, dissolvable granules, and liquid that are taken by mouth, each with different dosages, directions, and age limits. Extended-release tablets are taken every 12 hours, while the other forms are usually taken every 4 hours. Most people have few to no side effects when used as directed, but it can sometimes cause stomach upset, dizziness, and drowsiness.

### Indications for Mucinex DM

- Short-term relief of coughs caused by minor throat or lung irritation (e.g., common cold)
- Loosens and breaks up mucus in the airways (chest congestion)

### Pros and Cons for Mucinex DM

#### Pros

- Available as a tablet, oral liquid, and dissolvable granules
- Available over the counter without a prescription
- Sugar-free options available, so okay to use for people with high blood sugar
- Works within [30 minutes](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1527-3458.2007.00006.x) to help lessen cough

#### Cons

- Not meant to be used long-term
- Might need to take multiple times a day to relieve symptoms
- Many states require you to be [over 18](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4918034/) to buy it because of risk of misuse
- Can't cut or crush extended-release tablets

### Common Side Effects for Mucinex DM

- Side effects aren't common. See Other Side Effects.

### Warnings for Mucinex DM

- Risk of overdose and misuse
- Interactions with certain medications for Parkinson's disease and depression
- Caution use in people with phenylketonuria (PKU) - dissolvable granules only

### Summary for Delsym

Over-the-counter

Dextromethorphan (Delsym) is an over-the-counter [cough suppressant](https://www.goodrx.com/conditions/cough/whats-the-best-cough-medicine#otc-cough-medicines)(antitussive). It helps relieve ["dry" cough](https://www.goodrx.com/conditions/cough/can-i-ease-my-cough-without-a-prescription) in adults and children by suppressing the cough reflex. Dextromethorphan (Delsym) is available as an [extended-release (ER)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=bb0116d0-93e4-44e2-b0e4-c0b773eced6f&audience=consumer) cough syrup that's taken by mouth, [typically every 12 hours](https://www.goodrx.com/delsym/dosage). It also comes as an [immediate-release (IR)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a43d59f9-3a6c-4a7c-b98d-b86d6035f716&audience=consumer) caplet that's [usually taken every 6 to 8 hours](https://www.goodrx.com/delsym/dosage). Dextromethorphan might also come in additional formulations, under other brands. Some [common side effects of dextromethorphan (Delsym)](https://www.goodrx.com/dextromethorphan/dextromethorphan-side-effects) include nausea and stomach upset. Rarely, it can also make you sleepy.

### Indications for Delsym

- Short-term relief of [cough](https://www.goodrx.com/conditions/cough) caused by minor throat or lung irritation (e.g., common cold)

### Pros and Cons for Delsym

#### Pros

- Available as pills or oral liquids
- Sugar-free [options](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a43d59f9-3a6c-4a7c-b98d-b86d6035f716) available
- Available over the counter without a prescription

#### Cons

- Might need to take multiple times a day
- Meant for short-term treatment of cough only
- Found in many OTC products, so you can accidentally take too much

### Common Side Effects for Delsym

- [Nausea](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK538216/#_article-20426_s5_)
- Belly discomfort

### Warnings for Delsym

- Overdose and misuse
- Medication interactions
